steps: Curl your dominant hand into a flattened O, thumb and fingertips nearly touching.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of your torso as a landing pad.
Tap the flattened O hand down onto the flat palm once or twice.
Keep the tapping hand's palm facing down and the base palm facing up.
Keep a neutral face; the quick tap carries the whole meaning.
tip: The same sign as MONEY — context tells listeners you mean cash specifically.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, fingers together, like a tray.
Position it at chest height so the flat palm is a clear landing surface.
Shape your dominant hand into a C above the far edge of that palm.
Pull the C hand back toward yourself along the length of the flat palm.
Close the C into a loose S fist while it travels, as if grabbing coins.
Keep the base hand's palm facing up and your face neutral throughout.
tip: Sign it like EARN — a grab that brings pay toward your body.

steps: Close your non-dominant hand into an S fist and hold it at chest height.
Lay your dominant hand flat on top of that fist, fingers together.
Move the flat hand in a smooth circle on top of the fist.
Keep the flat hand's palm facing down while it circles.
Keep a neutral face; the circle outlines the region's boundary.
tip: Same sign as REGION — the circle traces the edge of an area.

steps: Sign SEE first: shape your dominant hand into a V, index and middle fingers extended.
Hold the V just below your eyes with the fingertips pointing forward.
Move the V hand straight outward away from your face.
Keep the V's palm facing inward toward your face during the move.
Then sign FINISH: brush your dominant flat hand downward across the other flat hand.
Keep a neutral face; FINISH marks the seeing as completed, like have seen.
tip: SEE plus FINISH — the added FINISH turns see into the perfect tense, have seen.

steps: Sign START: hold your non-dominant hand flat and upright in front of you.
Hook your dominant index finger against the edge of that flat hand.
Twist your dominant wrist in a small turn, as if turning a key.
Then sign PAST: raise your dominant flat hand beside your head.
Move the flat hand inward until it nearly touches your shoulder.
Keep the hand's palm facing your shoulder and your face neutral.
tip: Sign START, then the PAST marker — ASL marks past time with time signs, not word endings.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into a G, thumb pinched against the bent index finger.
Hold the G hand beside your temple, a few inches out from your head.
Draw one small circle in the air next to your temple.
Finish by touching the fingertips lightly against your temple.
Angle the G so the fingertips point toward your head with a calm, neutral face.
tip: Use the same sign as GOVERNMENT — it covers both the institution and the administration in power.
